purpose: Human-reviewed, source-grounded Phase 2B diagnostic set. Canonical concepts may be semantically entailed rather than literally named.

evidence.text: The Flay (E) active provides a brief displacement window that can interrupt channeled dashes like Tristana's Rocket Jump or Zac's Elastic Slingshot; time your E to hit the enemy at the apex of their dash animation to cancel their mobility entirely.

expected.subject: Thresh E
expected.condition: when Flay hits at the apex of the dash

expected.subject: Thresh E
expected.condition: when Flay hits at the apex of the dash

evidence.text: Rocket Jump (W) resets upon fully stacking Explosive Charge (E) or scoring a kill; in skirmishes, focus your E on the lowest health target to guarantee the reset, allowing for a secondary jump to reposition or chase.

expected.subject: Tristana E
expected.condition: when Explosive Charge is fully stacked

evidence.text: The E2 (Abduct) travel time creates a micro-window where you can buffer your W (Kingslayer) or an item active; casting W mid-dash ensures the heal and damage land immediately upon arrival, preventing the target from flashing away before your burst connects.

expected.subject: Sylas E
expected.condition: when Kingslayer is buffered during Abduct travel

evidence.text: Against champions like Lux, you must be intentional with your movement to bait out her E before you walk up to farm.

expected.subject: Lux E
expected.effect: opponent cannot safely walk up to farm

evidence.text: When playing against Lux, you must constantly track her E cooldown and bait it out, as she is essentially a one-spell champion who relies on that ability to poke and waveclear.
Against champions like Sylas, recognize that their ability to engage is tied to their E; if they miss it, they are effectively useless and you should play aggressively.
Caitlyn is a champion that wants to win lane by slow pushing, bombing enemies under their turret, and using her range advantage to pressure.

expected.subject: Caitlyn
expected.condition: when using range advantage with a slow push

evidence.text: Caitlyn is not a champion that excels in chaotic, explosive team fights where she is forced to fight multiple enemies at once; she prefers a controlled, front-to-back environment where she can poke and trap.
On Kai'Sa, you must be willing to use your W to fish for picks and create isolation opportunities rather than holding it indefinitely for a guaranteed kill.

expected.subject: Kai'Sa
expected.condition: when W is used to fish for picks

evidence.text: Kai'Sa is an opportunistic champion that needs to be ready to fight whenever a skirmish occurs, so she cannot afford to sit out of team fights due to poor mana management.

Tristana is a champion that wants to always have the angle to jump in, but she lacks the wave clear of champions like Jinx, meaning every auto-attack on a minion creates a window for the enemy to engage on her.

expected.subject: Tristana
expected.condition: when Tristana has an angle to jump in

evidence.text: If you are playing Alistar against a champion with a displacement ability like Thresh's Flay, wait for them to use that ability before committing to your W engage.

expected.subject: Thresh E
expected.effect: Alistar should not commit W engage

evidence.text: When fighting Aatrox, track his Q cooldowns; if he uses his Q1 and E, he cannot hit his Q2 if you stay on top of him.
When playing against Ezreal, prioritize pushing the wave to force him to use his Q on minions, which drains his mana and prevents him from poking you under your tower.

expected.subject: Ezreal
expected.condition: when Ezreal uses Q on minions

evidence.text: Against Viktor, recognize that his E poke is mana-inefficient and low-damage early; focus on baiting his Q-auto combo, as he is significantly weaker once his Q is on cooldown.

expected.subject: Viktor
expected.condition: early when Viktor E is used for poke

evidence.text: Yunara is a hyper-carry who is largely useless without her ultimate, so you must play around your ultimate cooldown and ensure you are healthy enough to all-in when it is available.

expected.subject: Yunara
expected.condition: when Yunara ultimate is available and she is healthy

evidence.text: Yunara does not have the shortest cooldowns, so you should hold your W to set up your support's crowd control rather than using it for minor poke.

expected.subject: Yunara
expected.condition: when Yunara holds W for support crowd control

evidence.text: Caitlyn is a poor champion to fight with when the enemy has a wave, as her E is harder to land and her Q deals less damage.
When playing against champions like Lux, bait their abilities by clicking into the wave, then move out to repeat the poke cycle.
Use biscuits when you are at the threshold of being killed, not when you are at full health, to maximize their healing efficiency.
When you are forced to recall, prioritize your gold threshold; if your base won't result in a meaningful item purchase, consider staying to farm or looking for a roam.
Do not initiate trades when the enemy has a shield available, as you will lose the trade and waste your own cooldowns.
League of Legends is a game of fighting on timers, such as spell cooldowns and wave states, rather than just a fighting game.
